reviewerRole: F1 navigation race fix reviewer, round 12

importantFindings.title: A save that closes its nested screen asynchronously goes Back a second time if the user has already gone Back. Save then Back lands two screens back.
importantFindings.location: src/navigation/nestedScreen.ts:66 (closeScreen) with src/features/boats/BoatManagement.tsx:712-716 (fault onSaved: await refresh(); closeScreen(detail))
importantFindings.scenario: Open a boat, tap Segnala, type a description and tap Salva avaria. Press the phone's Back (or the page's own Indietro) while createFault and refresh are still running. The Back lands on the boat detail. The save then calls closeScreen({detail}). closeScreen checks only that the nested key is present, and the boat-detail entry also has one, so it calls historyBack() again and the user ends on the boat list, not the boat detail. Probe b-double.probe.test.tsx (real BoatManagement, createFault taking 80 ms, one history.back() right after the click) ended with onDetail=false, onList=true, state=null. This is the same timing window as the Save-then-Home race that round 12 fixes, with Back in place of Home. afterPendingBack does not cover it because closeScreen, backStudentScreen and goBack still decide synchronously against a history.state that a pending or completed Back has already replaced. There is no data loss: the fault is saved.
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Make the close idempotent for the screen it closes. Pass or capture the screen being closed and call historyBack() only if stateRecord(history.state)[key] still equals that screen; otherwise setScreen(fallback) or do nothing. Run the check through afterPendingBack so it sees the landed entry. Apply the same check to backStudentScreen (StudentManagement.tsx:1290).

qolFindings.title: A queued openScreen or navigateStudentScreen still runs after its area has unmounted, leaving a phantom history entry that costs one dead Back
qolFindings.scenario: In Barche (list), tap the area's Back to Home (goBack, which calls historyBack), then tap a boat row before the popstate arrives. openScreen is queued. The Back lands on Home and BoatManagement unmounts. settleBack then pushes {...homeEntry, '__cvcHelperNested:boats': detail} and calls setScreen on the unmounted component. The user sees Home, but the next phone Back changes nothing visible. Harness probe c-phantom.probe.test.tsx: after settle, state={view:'home','__cvcHelperNested:boats':'detail'}; after one phone Back, still 'home'. Only reachable if the tap falls inside the popstate latency.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Inside the queued change, skip the push when the component is no longer mounted (an 'active' ref cleared in the effect cleanup), or when the landed entry no longer belongs to this area.

qolFindings.title: navigate's same-entry check reads the entry that a pending Back is leaving, so a tap can be lost or pushed as a duplicate
qolFindings.scenario: (a) On Equipaggi, tap the header Back (to Home) and then, before the popstate, tap the primary-nav Equipaggi. currentEntry.view is still 'crews', so navigate returns early and the user lands on Home: the tap is lost. (b) Tap the header Back and then Home before the popstate. The check passes (view is crews), and after landing pushView('home') pushes a second Home entry: one dead Back later. Only reachable inside the popstate latency.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Run the same-entry check inside the queued change (at the start of pushView, against the landed history.state), not before requestLeave/afterPendingBack.

qolFindings.title: When a Back's popstate never arrives, the 1 s fallback settles the queue but leaves passNextPop set, so the next phone Back skips the dialog-close and the leave guard
qolFindings.scenario: Case 1: historyBack() at the first history entry, so history.back() is a no-op. Case 2: an app Back whose popstate reaches no listener, e.g. AppShell unmounted by a course erase between historyBack and its popstate. The fallback runs the queued changes after about 1 s, but passNextPop stays true. The next phone Back is then taken as the app's own Back: it neither closes an open modal nor asks the guard, so on a StudentScan review with unsaved rows the review would be dropped without the discard question. Probe a-stale.probe.test.tsx: the queued change ran after 1001 ms, then a phone Back with an always-holding guard registered gave guard calls 0, held [false]. Production reachability is low: goBack, closeScreen and backStudentScreen normally have a previous entry.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: When settleBack runs from the fallback timer, also reset passNextPop (bind it to pendingBack) and, likewise, restoringUntil. Add unit tests for the fallback path and for a queued change whose component has unmounted; browserHistory.test.ts covers only the happy path.

qolFindings.title: pendingBack tracks a single Back: a second historyBack() before the first lands shares it, so the queue is released at the first popstate while the second Back is still in flight
qolFindings.scenario: Double-tap a nested screen's Back (two closeScreen calls both see the nested key and call historyBack twice), then tap Home. The first popstate consumes the boolean passNextPop and schedules settleBack. The queued Home push runs before the second Back lands, which can undo it: the original race. The second Back is also treated as a phone Back. Behaviour depends on the browser (jsdom collapses the two Backs into one), and three taps inside the traversal latency are needed.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Count the outstanding app Backs (passNextPop and pendingBack as a counter) and settle only when the count reaches zero, or queue a historyBack() issued while one is pending through afterPendingBack and re-check the landed entry.

evidenceInspected: src/navigation/browserHistory.ts (afterPendingBack, pendingBack, settleBack, historyBack, decideBack, requestLeave, useLeaveGuard, restoreCurrentEntry)
Leave guards in EvaluationManagement.tsx:390-412 and StudentScan.tsx:976-994; applyUpdate.ts

All history push/replace/back/forward call sites in src/ (all pushes now go through afterPendingBack; only restoreCurrentEntry's forward() and the synchronous close/goBack decisions are not serialized)
node_modules/jsdom SessionHistory.js (traversal is two setTimeout(0) tasks and it is a no-op at index 0)
